notes: Observation: landscape source dimensions are 2373 by 1690 pixels. Half a is 1246 by 1690 and half b is 1247 by 1690; bounding boxes in this report are always full-source coordinates.

Observation: the page contains mathematical labels/formulas and six freehand figures, with no running prose, title, date, or linguistic accents. No manuscript folio is established. The bottom-left 3 is retained only as an archive-sheet comment.
Observation: upper rows relate Ob/Fl expressions with two short ascending arrows and a heavily retraced right arrow, plus a crossed term and an unstruck replacement.

Observation: the middle rows extend products with a terminal Ob factor; the final such factor in the n-row is struck. The source’s surprising index and operator shapes have not been repaired from the pattern.

Observation: the lower rows show inclusions, products, starred pairs, and an amalgamation expression. The author’s explicit question is transcribed verbatim as “(-?)”. No written verbal question or assertion appears.

Observation: pale background remnants show through much of the sheet. No complete readable typed block or recoverable sequence of background words was identified. H’s claim that the reverse is a typescript is editorial metadata, not evidence for invented text. The sheet is inventoried as text rather than reused_typed on the visible evidence.
Observation: tiny detached dark flecks next to two Fl expressions and two multiplication signs are preserved graphically without asserting that they are punctuation, primes or exponents.

Observation: the two roof-like accents at the isolated inclusion and final amalgamation member differ visibly from the short diagonal dot above the amalgamation subscript. These occurrences are not normalized to a single accent.

Uncertainty: overwrite order in the third-row index and in several O/F composites cannot be recovered fully from static ink. Retained deleted forms are diplomatic representations of visible underlying contours, with local doubts where the letters themselves are not secure.
Verification scope: no proof, re-proof, computation or formal mathematical check was performed. Formula-pattern observations are descriptive only; no statement was used as a mathematical premise.

Reader logistics: the first attempt to view crop 13 failed with exec-server transport closed before any image was delivered. The same saved crop was requested again, without recropping; crops 13 and 14 were then delivered once. No other image was re-viewed.
Reader output: only this reader directory was written. No OCR, web source, parallel text, other scan, other reader output, compilation or subagent was used.

Final text-only validation: compared reading.tex against C once; every substantive change is logged. Inline literal-trace TikZ baselines were then expressed relative to their own bounding boxes to avoid source-coordinate layout offsets. No content or image decision changed.

notation.ink: Doubled F is used only at inspected occurrences with an enclosed white channel between a return stroke and a main upright. Crops 03,05,07,09,11,12,13,18,19,20 document these. Single-stem triangular upper arms alone, such as the first Fl in the F_3 row, are not automatically doubled. This is a graphic transcription, not an inferred uniform alphabet.
The l is looped; the following 0 is a low rounded mark. Parentheses and inner C can overlap or loop. The top-right argument remains C_1|C_n.
O is a closed or nearly closed oval and b has a tall upright with a right lower return. Old F/Fl strokes survive within some live O shapes.
Top C index has an upright below a transverse bar and a left rising piece. The terminal Ob factors contain matching 4-shaped low forms.
3 has a two-bend terminal descent; n is a low shoulder. The last-pair O index contains both kinds of trace and is retained as 3|n.
The relation after F_n is connected, with curved upper segment, oblique descent and short low foot. It is recorded as 2|=, not regularized from the F_3 row.
The third argument in the F_3 row is a complete tall closed loop with a lower crossing/return, matching the preceding l rather than open C.
The isolated inclusion and final amalgamation member have roof/caret-shaped raised marks. The amalgamation subscript has one short diagonal dot. All three were independently examined.
Two uprights on a common baseline extending left of the first upright; this shape occurs once cancelled near the top and once live near the bottom.

Ordinary crosses have two diagonals; the lower pair operators have six rays; continuations are single horizontal runs, not dot ellipses. Detached marks by lower crosses are literally traced without a semantic prime assignment.

First low loop remains 0|empty-set because diagonal connector ink crosses it. Second low upright is 1. Connector has two low returns, a parallel short stroke near the first X, and a detached fleck above/left of the second.

Square corner knots have tiny white counters, with two at lower-left. Lens endpoint knots are dark without a secure counter. Attached pegs, disconnected stroke ends and detached upper prism dash are kept distinct.

brief_feedback: The workflow was sufficient. A practical unresolved convention is how much of a cursive F return is required to count as a doubled alphabet: I used an actually enclosed white upright channel, documented occurrence by occurrence, rather than normalizing whole formulas. One transport failure required obtaining the identical saved crop again; no additional crop or repeat inspection resulted.
